notes.text: A 12-inch skillet holds 8 eggs. For more than 4, cook the eggs in two skillets side by side, or in two batches.

move.title: Eggs cooked in salsa
move.body: Poaching means cooking food gently in hot liquid. Today the liquid is salsa: you'll simmer it in a pan, slide eggs into it, and cover them until they're set. They go on crisp corn tortillas with warm refried beans.

callback.body: If you made shakshuka, you've done this: eggs set in a gently bubbling sauce under a lid. Salsa works the same way, and it's faster because the sauce comes from a jar.

why.title: Low heat for eggs
why.body: Eggs turn rubbery when they get blasted with heat. A gentle simmer under a lid cooks the whites and yolks all the way through while they stay tender. If the salsa bubbles hard, turn the heat down.

why.title: Why the lid
why.body: The bottom of the egg sits in the hot salsa, but the top only sees air. A lid traps steam, and the steam cooks the top of the egg at the same time as the bottom.

why.title: Crisp tortillas hold up
why.body: A soft tortilla goes soggy under beans and salsa. A minute in a hot pan with a little oil makes it crisp, so it holds everything without falling apart.

wrong.sign: The whites are still clear and runny
wrong.fix: Put the lid back on and cook 2 more minutes on low, then check again.
The heat is too high. Turn it down to low before the eggs go in.
Crisp them a little longer next time, and add the beans and eggs just before eating.

quiz.q: Why does the pan get a lid?
choices: Steam cooks the top of the eggs
quiz.explain: The lid traps steam, so the top of each egg cooks along with the bottom.

quiz.q: How hot do the eggs need to be?
quiz.explain: Eggs are safe at 160°F: whites and yolks set.

steps.text: Open the beans and scrape them into the small saucepan with a splash of water. Warm them over low heat, stirring now and then, while you crisp the tortillas.
steps.tip: Keep your fingers away from the cut edge of the lid. It's as sharp as a knife.

steps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Lay in 2 tortillas and cook until crisp and spotted brown, flipping once with the tongs. Move them to a paper-towel-lined plate. Do the rest the same way, adding a little oil each time.
Turn off the beans. Wipe out the skillet with a paper towel, pour in the salsa, and heat it over medium heat until it bubbles gently.
steps.tip: Fold the paper towel and hold it with the tongs. The pan is hot.

steps.text: Turn the heat down to low. Use the back of the spoon to make a little well in the salsa for each egg ({n:egg} in all). Crack each egg into the small bowl, then slide it into a well.
steps.tip: Cracking into a bowl first keeps shell out of the pan.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and wipe the counter where the eggs were.
Cover the pan and cook on low until the whites and yolks are set all the way through.
steps.look: The whites are solid white, and the yolks are firm when you touch them with the spoon.

steps.text: Slide the thermometer sideways into an egg. It needs to read at least 160°F before anyone eats. If it doesn't, cover the pan for 2 more minutes and check again.
Turn off the heat. Slice the avocado and chop the cilantro if you're using them.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front.

steps.text: Put 2 crisp tortillas on each plate and spread them with beans. Lift the eggs out with the spatula, with some salsa, and set them on top. Add avocado, cilantro, and queso fresco if you're using them.
steps.tip: The handle stays hot for a long time. Leave an oven mitt on it so nobody grabs it bare-handed.
